statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt is now twenty-six hours old and removes the very price path this score measures. Stress firms to 57 in the elevated band after a material verification this hour: CME FedWatch pricing for a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC has reached roughly 87%, up from 72% a day earlier and 50% a week ago, after August CPI held at 3.4% with core at 0.3% month over month. Confidence is 87 in the high band: index level, VIX, H.15 yields, crude and the seven-day calendar were each re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the only structurally unavailable input is live price path.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support that reading. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 across twenty-three of the twenty-four published slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, which is this horizon's final slot. A score that measures a pathological price path cannot be elevated across hours in which no path can form. Second, the last observed session granted mean reversion rather than denying it, and did so against a hawkish input: August CPI printed with core slightly hot, hike odds jumped, and the index still closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point range, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. Third, the weekend escalation that supports Stress is a supply-route story rather than observed index structure, and it is partly offset by Friday's 2.37% fall in crude on signs of Hormuz diplomacy, by Saudi non-retaliation at Baghdad's request, and by Monday's scheduled Salalah meeting. A narrow danger window is published for the Sunday reopen hour and the hour after it, the only part of this horizon in which an instrument trades. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unchanged.
headline: Twenty-six hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while verification this hour puts CME FedWatch at roughly 87% for a Wednesday rate hike after August CPI held at 3.4%, and the Saudi East-West pipeline carrying 4% to 5% of global oil supply stays shut with Houthi forces holding Perim island and the Bab el-Mandeb exit into Sunday's 22:00 UTC reopen.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX is 15.84, down 2.00 points or 11.21% from 17.84, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 5-year at 4.75%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up 9.7% on the week and 20.15% on the month, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

The material new verification this hour concerns Wednesday's FOMC rather than the Middle East. August CPI, released Friday, rose 0.4% on the month for a 3.4% annual rate in line with estimates, while core accelerated 0.3% on the month, slightly above expectations. Rate-hike pricing responded far more than equities did: CME FedWatch moved to roughly 87% for a 25 basis point increase on Wednesday, from 72% the previous day and 50% a week earlier, and reporting notes that three FOMC members had already dissented in favour of higher rates. The equity response was the opposite of stressed, with all eleven S&P 500 sectors green and every megacap higher, and the indices nevertheless closed the week lower after a four-day losing streak. This combination matters for the scoring: a hawkish repricing that the index absorbed constructively is Stress and Confidence evidence, not Tail evidence, and a decision discounted at 87% carries materially less unpriced surprise than the same decision carried a week ago.

The supply picture is unchanged from the previous hour and remains the second Stress input. The Saudi East-West pipeline to Yanbu, which had been moving between 4% and 5% of global oil supplies, is still shut after drone strikes launched from Iraq, with no published restart date, while Houthi forces hold Mokha, Dhubab and Perim island and have threatened to close Bab el-Mandeb entirely. With Hormuz blockaded since February, the principal bypass is impaired at both its inlet and its Red Sea exit. The offsets are real and verified: crude fell 2.37% on Friday on signs of Hormuz diplomacy, Yemen's defence ministry reported counterattacks against Houthi targets, Riyadh has withheld retaliation, and foreign ministers from the GCC, Iraq and Iran are due in Salalah on Monday, with Iran's president signalling intent to sign an Oman navigation agreement.

The assessment consequence is that Tail stays at 6 while Stress firms to 57. Twenty-three of the twenty-four published slots contain no tradeable instrument, and event importance, hike pricing and headline severity raise Stress and Confidence rather than Tail until an actual price path is observable. The exception is the final slot. Sunday's 22:00 UTC reopen is the one hour in this horizon in which a price path can form, and it combines structurally thin liquidity with a two-day accumulation of unpriced headlines, so conditional Tail steps to 21 there and the mapped state for that slot is WATCH. A narrow danger window covering that hour and the one after it is published accordingly. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context was reviewed but was both stale at more than two hours old and flagged partial, so it was not relied upon.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 23:00 UTC on 11 September to 22:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens two hours into the CME halt with Tail at 6 and Stress at 62, still decaying from Friday's session. Tail fell to 5 by 00:00 UTC and has held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across every remaining slot, tracking the closure rather than any directional view, which is the correct behaviour for a score that measures price path when no price path exists. Stress decayed steadily from 62 to a 50 trough at 17:00 UTC as the initial pipeline shock was absorbed, then firmed through 52 and 53 to 56 in the final slot as the Bab el-Mandeb seizure and the U.S. attribution of the pipeline attack were verified. Confidence held a narrow 85 to 88 range throughout. Every slot mapped to EA_ON and green, and no danger window was published in any of them.
outlookSummary: Twenty-three of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract reopens at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, which is this horizon's final slot. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then drifts gradually to 18 through the closure as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates, and steps to 21 in the reopen hour, the one slot in which a price path can actually form. That single slot maps to WATCH and yellow; every other slot stays in the low band and maps to EA_ON and green. A narrow danger window is published across the reopen hour and the hour after it rather than a broad session-wide caution. Stress traces a shallow U, easing to 54 across the dead overnight hours and firming to 64 by the reopen as pre-positioning meets an unresolved supply picture and a near-certain Wednesday hike. Two genuine intra-horizon checkpoints exist. Tadawul opens at 07:00 UTC and provides the first live pricing anywhere of the pipeline shutdown and the Bab el-Mandeb seizure, though as Saudi cash equity it informs Stress and Confidence without establishing index price-path evidence. The reopen itself is the second, and the conditional invalidation there is straightforward: an orderly two-sided first few hours would return Tail to the low band, while repeated extension after failed retracements would be the first genuine Tail evidence of the weekend. Confidence dips to 85 through the quietest hours and rebuilds to 87 as Sunday reporting refreshes the evidence base.

Stress stays 56 on an unresolved supply picture: with Hormuz blockaded since February, the Yanbu bypass shut and Bab el-Mandeb under Houthi control, the main workaround is impaired at both ends.
